title: request_transformer plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `request_transformer` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component RequestTransformerConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

operation.description:
add: insert if absent (does not overwrite).
update: write, creating intermediate objects as needed.
remove: delete the field.
rename: move old → new, with rollback if the destination is unreachable.
Operation-incompatible extras are rejected: only add/update
may set `value`; only rename may set `new_key`; remove may
set neither.

key.description:
Dot-notation body path. Supports nested objects
('user.address.city'), array indexing via numeric segments
('items.0.name'), and backslash-escaped literal dots
('meta.weird\\.key'). Empty segments (an empty path, or a
leading, trailing, or doubled unescaped `.`) are rejected.
`rename` additionally rejects unescaped numeric segments here
and in `new_key`.

value.description:
Required for add/update; must not be set for remove/rename.
Accepts any JSON value — strings, numbers, booleans, objects,
arrays, and explicit null.
Strings that parse as JSON (e.g., "42", "true", '{"a":1}')
are inserted as the parsed type at runtime; otherwise kept
as a JSON string.

new_key.description:
Required for rename; must not be set for add/update/remove.
Array indices and empty dot-segments are rejected in a rename
`key` / `new_key`.

RequestTransformerConfig.description:
Plugin: request_transformer — Modifies request headers, query params,
and JSON body. Configuration is fail-closed: unknown top-level keys
and unknown per-rule keys are rejected at plugin load time. Header
and query rules enforce operation-exact fields (only add/update
accept `value`; only rename accepts `new_key`; remove accepts
neither). Every configured header `value` must be a valid HTTP
`HeaderValue` (same complete syntax accepted at H1/H2/H3 emission),
including rejection of CR/LF and other forbidden control bytes.
Unknown operations / targets and missing required fields are also
rejected. Every rule must set an explicit `target` (`header`,
`query`, or `body`); there is no default.

When `apply_route_overrides: true`, the plugin accepts an empty `rules`
array so it can participate in the chain-level route-header final
phase for per-rule transforms published by `mesh_route_dispatch` onto
`RequestContext.route_override_request_transform`. Every enabled
instance applies only its static `rules` first; proxy core then applies
the matched route list exactly once after the last eligible instance —
route-level header writes win under multiple same-type instances and
priority overrides. The Istio VirtualService translator auto-emits a
proxy-scoped instance with `rules: []` + `apply_route_overrides: true`
on routes that carry `headers.request.{set,add,remove}` and have no
operator-configured `request_transformer`. That exact translator-owned
consumer — generated id, proxy scope and ownership, empty `rules`, and
`apply_route_overrides: true` — is ADDITIVE: a same-name global
transformer keeps its operator-authored header / query / body rules, so
a VS-translated route does not silently lose them and no shadowing
warning is emitted for it. An ordinary operator-configured proxy-scoped
instance keeps the normal proxy-replaces-global contract.

At least one of a non-empty `rules` array or `apply_route_overrides:
true` is required: a config with no effect is rejected at plugin load
time. Per-operation required and forbidden properties are modelled in
the target-specific rule schemas below. Operation-incompatible extras
are rejected by PRESENCE, so an explicit `null` fails exactly as a
string would; explicit `null` on an optional top-level field is
accepted and treated as absent.

apply_route_overrides.description:
When `true`, this instance accepts an empty `rules` array and
participates in the chain-level request route-header finalization
phase for transforms published by `mesh_route_dispatch`. The plugin
declares `modifies_request_headers() == true` so the dispatcher
allocates a separate cloned header map for route-level writes
(preserving the gateway invariant that `ctx.headers` carries the
original inbound headers during `before_proxy`). Auto-emitted by the
Istio VirtualService translator. Explicit `null` is accepted and
treated as `false`.

runtime_overlay_scope.description: Optional RTDS boolean key controlling whether the transformer runs. Must contain at least one non-whitespace character; surrounding whitespace is trimmed at runtime. Explicit `null` is accepted and treated as absent.

default_enabled.description: Fallback when `runtime_overlay_scope` is configured but the accepted RTDS overlay has no boolean value for that key. Explicit `null` is accepted and treated as absent (so the `true` default applies).

runtime_overlay_resolved_enabled.description: Reserved, mesh-managed. Mesh slice preparation writes the accepted RTDS overlay's value for `runtime_overlay_scope` here, so the gate is validated, built, and published in the same request generation as the rules it gates (GHSA-83rc-23c9-3g9x). The plugin resolves one immutable decision at construction and every request phase reads it, so the gate is never re-evaluated mid-request. Ignored without `runtime_overlay_scope`, and rewritten authoritatively on every mesh apply — operators should not set it by hand; an explicitly authored value simply acts as a static pin outside mesh mode.

operation.description:
add: insert if absent (does not overwrite). Note: this is
the historical Ferrum semantics, not Istio's "append to
multi-value" semantics — use `update` to overwrite.
update: write the header value.
remove: delete the header.
rename: move old → new header name.
Operation-incompatible extras are rejected: only add/update
may set `value`; only rename may set `new_key`; remove may
set neither.

key.description:
HTTP header name; must be a complete HTTP field-name token (the
same grammar `HeaderName` accepts). Add/update destinations and
rename destinations
reject gateway-owned names (case-insensitive, with `_` treated as
`-`, so `X_Forwarded_For` and `content_length` are refused too):
host, content-length,
connection, transfer-encoding, keep-alive, proxy-authorization,
proxy-connection, te, trailer, upgrade, expect, x-forwarded-for,
x-forwarded-proto, x-forwarded-host,
x-ferrum-original-content-encoding, and x-grpc-web-mode. They also
reject every name in the gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` consumer
assertion namespace (including x-consumer-username and
x-consumer-custom-id) and in the router's `x-path-param-*`
route-capture namespace (either spelling); the error names the
rule.
Removal and rename sources remain allowed, except for the
gateway-owned x-ferrum-hops proxy hop count (either spelling):
every rule that names it, as key or new_key, is rejected.
Use preserve_host_header for Host or trusted-proxy configuration
for forwarding identity.

value.description:
Required for add/update; must not be set for remove/rename.
Must be a valid HTTP HeaderValue (HTAB, visible ASCII, and
obs-text are accepted; CR, LF, DEL, and other C0 controls are
rejected).
May reference up to 8 request variables, compiled at load time:
`$(consumer.username)`, `$(client_ip)`, `$(request_id)`,
`$(header.<name>)` and `$(query.<name>)` (both read from the
ORIGINAL client request, so a rename cannot relabel a
credential). `$$(` writes a literal `$(`; an unknown variable, an
unterminated `$(`, or a credential-bearing source name (the
built-in credential headers in any `_` / `-` spelling, or any
name the shared sensitive-name classifier flags: `*token*`,
`*secret*`, `password`, `api_key`, …) is rejected. When a
variable is unavailable for a request — or names a credential
location an auth plugin marked — or the resolved text is not a
valid HeaderValue, the rule is skipped for that request and
`request_transformer.rule_skipped` transaction metadata records
`template_unresolved` / `template_invalid_header_value`.

new_key.description:
Required for rename; must not be set for add/update/remove.
Must be a complete HTTP field-name token and must not be a
gateway-owned destination listed under key.

operation.description:
add: append if the decoded name is absent (does not overwrite;
existing duplicates are left untouched).
update: rewrite every matching decoded-name pair's value, or
append when absent.
remove: delete every matching decoded-name pair.
rename: rename every matching pair, preserving value encoding
and key-without-equals shape; existing destination names stay.
Mutations apply to an ordered, duplicate-aware representation of
the retained raw query after authentication-owned credential
pairs (`auth.strip_query_param.*`) are removed from that input,
and are published as the outbound query for every primary
backend URL builder and request_mirror. The proxy still applies
a final strip pass as defense in depth. A rename/update of a
marked credential name therefore cannot relocate the secret.
Operation-incompatible extras are rejected: only add/update
may set `value`; only rename may set `new_key`; remove may
set neither.

key.description:
Query parameter name matched after percent-decoding. Must not
contain CR or LF.

value.description:
Required for add/update; must not be set for remove/rename.
Must not contain CR or LF. Authored onto the outbound query with
RFC 3986 percent-encoding (`%20` for spaces, never `+`). Accepts
the same `$(...)` request variables as a header `value`; the
resolved text is percent-encoded like any authored value.

new_key.description:
Required for rename; must not be set for add/update/remove.
Must not contain CR or LF.

TransformerBodyRenamePath.description:
A dot-notation body path usable as a `rename` source or destination.
Array indices are rejected at plugin load time: rename over an array is
ambiguous (move? swap? overwrite?) and `Vec::remove`'s leftward shift
would silently drop a trailing element. Use `remove` + `add` to relocate
an array element. An ESCAPED numeric segment (`counts\.0` — a literal
key named `counts.0`) remains valid, so the exclusion applies only to an
unescaped path whose dot-delimited segments contain a plain integer.

TransformerOperationFieldExactness.description:
The operation-exact field contract both transformers enforce at plugin
load time, shared by every header / query / body rule schema: `add` and
`update` require `value` and forbid `new_key`; `rename` requires
`new_key` and forbids `value`; `remove` forbids both. Forbidden
properties are rejected by PRESENCE, so an explicit `null` fails exactly
as a string would. A body `value` may itself be `null` on `add` /
`update` — that sets the target field to JSON null.
